transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (NovaOps Head of ML), Maya Rodriguez (CTO), Liam O'Connell (SRE), Sofia Herrera (Product), Arjun Patel (Localization PM)

Summary: (auto) high-level alignment on pilot scope, target SLOs, model quality expectations across English + Spanish + German + Japanese, and operational constraints for a private or dedicated pilot.

00:00:03 Alex Chen: Hey, everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we'll go through what success looks like, workload numbers, model options, and then a bench plan. Priya and I will take notes and follow up.
00:00:20 Daniel Park: Sounds good. Minute — for context, we've been using a mix of commercial APIs for NLU and some internal heuristics, but cost is exploding and we need better latency at scale. We also need consistent output across languages.
00:00:40 Maya Rodriguez: And top priority for us is reliability and data controls — we can't send all logs externally, so private deployment is on the table. but we want to see tradeoffs.
00:01:05 Priya Nair: Great. quick clarifying Q: When you say "consistent output across languages", is that for operator notes, incident summaries, or automated command generation?
00:01:20 Daniel Park: Primarily incident summaries and operator-facing runbooks. sometimes translation of operator notes from local ops teams. Need to preserve technical terms and acronyms.
00:01:38 Alex Chen: OK, success criteria — let's make these explicit. Daniel, Maya — does the following capture it? 1) mean latency (p95) under 500ms for 256-token responses in hosted mode, 2) accuracy/ROUGE-like quality thresholds on our eval set >= baseline vendor, 3) cost per 1k tokens under $X for pilot target, and 4) multilingual parity (EN/ES/DE/JP) within a small delta of EN baseline.
00:02:05 Daniel Park: That seems right, though we might push p95 to 300ms if feasible. Our primary user SLA is 300-500ms.
00:02:20 Priya Nair: 300ms p95 for 256 tokens is ambitious on some models; with quantized 70B families you might hit it with dedicated GPUs and prefilling caches, but cost goes up. We'll discuss tradeoffs.
00:02:40 Sofia Herrera: For workload sizing, here's where we are — 120 concurrent operator sessions during peak, average 3 requests per session per minute, average response length ~200 tokens, and some longer generation tasks (500-1k tokens) for detailed runbooks maybe 10% of traffic.
00:03:05 Alex Chen: Good, so ballpark qps: 120 sessions * 3 rps ~ 360 rps? that's high — I think per minute vs per second got mixed. can you confirm per minute?
00:03:20 Sofia Herrera: Sorry, per minute — I meant 3 requests per minute per session. so peak concurrent 120 => 6 rps. averaged across the day 2 rps.
00:03:35 Priya Nair: That clarifies — so peak around 6 rps, but bursty patterns when incidents happen. important for batching and autoscaling behavior.
00:03:50 Daniel Park: Also, many calls are short prompts for quick summaries (50-150 tokens). we'll provide a distribution.
00:04:05 Alex Chen: OK. For the pilot we'll simulate a 2x amplification for incident spikes to validate autoscale.
00:04:20 Liam O'Connell: On infra constraints: we prefer VPC/private deployment for data residency; however for the first benchmark we can use hosted endpoints if Redwood can guarantee token-level logging disabled and not stored. we'll document firewall needs.
00:04:45 Priya Nair: We have a checklist for private vs dedicated. For hosted we have options: no-persist logging, or bring-your-own-key with KMS. For private, we'll need an agent or peering connection; we'll work with your SRE on port and IP allowlists.
00:05:10 Alex Chen: Model shortlist — based on initial intake we propose testing three open-model families: 1) LLaMA-2-chat 13B (quantized plan), 2) Mistral-Instruct 7B (opt-weight), and 3) Falcon-40B or comparable 33-40B candidate. We can substitute a 70B quantized variant if you want higher quality to compare latency/cost.
00:05:40 Daniel Park: Why not include 70B out of the box? our quality bar is fairly high for domain-specific jargon.
00:05:52 Priya Nair: 70B variants generally yield better long-form coherence and technical term fidelity, but they increase memory and cost. we can include a 70B-quantized run as a delta test to understand quality vs cost. Also the Mistral 7B has strong multilingual capabilities, surprisingly good on en/es, but may struggle on japanese structural nuance.
00:06:20 Arjun Patel: On Japanese, we need honorifics and domain-specific terms consistent — losing nuance can lead to bad operator instructions. can you evaluate morphological fidelity?
00:06:33 Priya Nair: We'll include targeted evaluation for Japanese tokenization and term preservation. we'll use bilingual reference sets and a small human eval panel for subjective judgment.
00:06:50 Sofia Herrera: How do you propose to measure "term preservation"? string match? embedding similarity? human check?
00:07:00 Priya Nair: combination — exact match for key entities, embedding cosine for paraphrase acceptance, and a small set of human ratings for critical cases. We'll provide the rubric.
00:07:15 Alex Chen: Metrics we should instrument in the benchmark: latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, success rate (no hallucination triggers flagged by heuristics), cost per 1k tokens, and multilingual quality deltas.
00:07:35 Daniel Park: On hallucinations — we have a set of 120 "safety" prompts that historically trigger errors; include those.
00:07:45 Priya Nair: Noted. Benchmark plan: we'll run a controlled suite — 1) a functional eval on 500 prompts (mixture of languages and lengths) for quality, 2) a load test simulating 2x peak bursts for 15 minutes to measure autoscale and tail latency, 3) a long-form generation test on 100 prompts of 500-1k tokens to see memory/throughput behavior.
00:08:20 Alex Chen: For numbers: we'll provision a baseline test for each model variant with 1k sample runs for quality, and for load test generate a 15-minute stream at peak shape. Expected run time for bench ~4-6 hours across all models if we sequence them.
00:08:38 Daniel Park: That's OK. Our target pilot window is 6 weeks: week 0 sign off, week 1-2 benching and tuning, week 3 pilot ingest + smoke tests, week 4-6 live evaluation with telemetry.
00:08:58 Maya Rodriguez: We need a go/no-go checkpoint after benching to decide private vs hosted pilot. if bench shows hosted meets SLOs and security controls, we might do hosted initially.
00:09:12 Alex Chen: Makes sense. On measurement tooling — Priya, we'll use Redwood's trace and cost tooling plus your own telemetry. Priya: any special instrumentation to add?
00:09:25 Priya Nair: We'll add token-level timing, batch sizes, cache-hit rates to the benchmark logs. also capture KV-cache warm vs cold behavior on repeated prompts.
00:09:40 Liam O'Connell: For private deployment tests we will need an isolated corridor — we'll provide an account with peered VPC and a test cluster. verify IP and port ranges.
00:09:55 Alex Chen: We'll send a checklist and a sample infra diagram.
00:10:05 Daniel Park: Quick question on quantization — what quant levels are you recommending? 4-bit, 5-bit?
00:10:15 Priya Nair: Our typical plan is: try 4-bit q4_0 for memory savings on 13B/70B if available, but 4-bit can slightly degrade some nuanced outputs. For critical domains we recommend q5_1 or 5-bit variants for a better quality/cost sweet spot. We'll include both in the bench.
00:10:38 Arjun Patel: Is there a way to do mixed approach — 13B quantized for routine prompts and 70B for long-form or safety-critical generation?
00:10:49 Priya Nair: Yes, that's a common routing policy — short fast paths route to smaller models, long/safety-critical to larger variants. Redwood supports automated fallbacks and routing policies we can preconfigure for pilot.
00:11:05 Alex Chen: Regarding costs, we'll provide a modeled cost per 1k tokens for each variant including expected token mix. Daniel, what's your budget guardrail?
00:11:17 Daniel Park: We have a soft ceiling for pilot of $12k/month including infra and licensing. we can flex if quality is materially better.
00:11:28 Alex Chen: We'll run cost curves and show tradeoffs.
00:11:33 Sofia Herrera: For human evals — we can provide bilingual SMEs for Spanish and German; will Redwood coordinate the Japanese raters?
00:11:44 Priya Nair: We can recommend vendors or use your internal team. we'll provide the rubric and a small annotation interface export.
00:11:55 Maya Rodriguez: SOC2/ISO and audit logs — we need proof for procurement. Alex, can you attach the compliance pack?
00:12:05 Alex Chen: Yes, I'll attach SOC2 and data processing addendum links in the follow-up.
00:12:12 Daniel Park: One more — latency targets in private deployment may be stricter; we need to know the expected difference compared to hosted. any ballparks?
00:12:25 Priya Nair: Private with dedicated GPUs on-prem will have lower network hop variance but depends on your infra. typical delta is +-50ms network; GPU queuing is the bigger factor based on model size and batching. We'll quantify in the bench.
00:12:45 Alex Chen: Recap of agreed pilot: 6-week window, bench week of 2027-01-05, model shortlist (13B, 7B, 40/70B run), metrics instrumentation, private vs hosted decision post-bench, deliverables and artifacts as in action items.
00:13:05 Daniel Park: Great. we'll get the prompts and confirm the bench slot.
00:13:20 Maya Rodriguez: and procurement — we'll need an MSA; can you attach standard terms?
00:13:30 Alex Chen: yes, will send standard pilot MSA and pricing tiers.
00:13:38 Sofia Herrera: small ask — can you include a short demo of failover behavior if model pool is saturated?
00:13:48 Priya Nair: We'll include a short failover demo and routing policy doc in the follow-up.
00:14:00 Arjun Patel: Also we need to test localized tokenization for Japanese/Multibyte, please ensure your harness handles utf8 and token counts correctly.
00:14:12 Priya Nair: noted. we'll include tokenization sanity tests.
00:14:25 Alex Chen: Any other questions?
00:14:30 Daniel Park: Not from me. thanks.
00:14:35 Maya Rodriguez: Nope.
00:14:38 Liam O'Connell: all good.
00:14:40 Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the deck, benchmark template, and security docs.
00:14:50 (meeting informal wrap)

Notes on noise and transcription: some speaker labels may be imperfect; occasional filler words and small word swaps (e.g., "cache" transcribed as "cash") are expected in raw transcript.

End of transcript.
file_notes: Pilot scoped for 6 weeks; emphasis on multilingual fidelity and domain-term preservation. Unique aspects: low QPS but high burstiness; mixed short/long generation; strict private deployment preference tied to procurement. Recommended to include both 13B quantized and a 70B quantized delta to measure quality uplift vs cost.
